source.title: Fixing Weight Decay Regularization in Adam

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. Its body title differs from the provided metadata title; no other document problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: Compares Adam with L2 regularization to Adam with decoupled weight decay and reports held-out performance; this tests the adaptive-optimizer generalization version using a different regularization comparison.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports comparisons across three learning-rate schedules; exact test-error values are shown only in figures. Results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: This is an original source for V4's decoupled-weight-decay qualification. Its image-classification experiments compare Adam, AdamW and momentum SGD using held-out error, showing that changing regularization can substantially close the optimizer performance gap.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: decoupled weight decay substantially improves Adam's generalization relative to L2 regularization and makes it competitive with momentum SGD on the tested image datasets. The authors also emphasize easier hyperparameter tuning and improved anytime performance with warm restarts, while calling for verification on more tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Tests a change to Adam's regularization implementation (decoupled weight decay versus L2 regularization), rather than the broader optimizer comparisons and benchmark set in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning-rate schedule changes the outcome: AdamW outperforms Adam for fixed, drop-step, and cosine schedules, with larger differences for better schedules. Training budget and dataset also vary in the reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Collaborator-supplied EEG comparisons report AdamW accuracy of 73.68% versus Adam's 71.37% for Deep4Net, and 72.04% versus 61.34% for ResNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoupled weight decay can improve Adam's held-out accuracy on intracranial EEG classification with the same hyperparameter setting.

record.problems: The core comparisons in Figures 1 and 3 and the ImageNet32x32 supplement provide exact values only in figures; the text reports qualitative comparisons. No uncertainty estimates are stated for those comparisons. The EEG comparisons are reported as supplied by collaborators.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant result rows left out.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Generalization as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.
Own experiments on language benchmarks, word-level language modeling, adaptive optimizers other than Adam, broad optimizer-specific tuning, and switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets; batch size is held at 128.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size or augmentation.
Sharpness measurements and their association with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: Direct optimizer comparison: after 100 epochs on CIFAR-10, the best Adam settings perform clearly worse than the best momentum-SGD settings, whereas the best AdamW settings rival SGD and SGDW. These comparisons establish both the original gap and its recovery.

With warm restarts, the Adam variants close most of the gap to SGDWR on CIFAR-10 and achieve comparable performance on ImageNet32x32. Existing rows record only AdamW versus Adam, omitting this direct comparison with SGD.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are assigned because arXiv:1711.05101 is an explicitly listed original source for V4. Figure-only numerical values cannot be reconstructed from the supplied text; the reported directions are explicitly supported by the prose. The supplied body title matches the listed original title.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation are not tested.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures are not compared.
Language benchmarks, broad hyperparameter tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models are not tested.
Sharpness and other generalization measures are not tested.
Removing memorized training examples is not tested.
